purpose: Encode and decode 8 strain-tensor orientation states in diamond-cubic Si, indexed by the <111> bond directions.
supersedes: v1.0 — see audit_v1. The 8-state / 3-bit result stands; its derivation and its read/write mechanism did not.
name_note: The name is retained for continuity but is misleading. Octahedral COORDINATION is 6-fold; an octahedron has 6 VERTICES (log2 6 = 2.585 bits, not 3). What supplies 8 is the octahedron's 8 FACES, whose normals lie along <111> — the same directions as the dual cube's vertices, and the sp3 bond directions of diamond-cubic Si. Consider renaming to Bond_Direction_State_Encoder.

geometry_basis.derivation: 4 sp3 bond directions of sublattice A, union 4 of sublattice B. The two sets are related by the inversion centre at the bond midpoint (pairwise 180 deg apart) and their union is the complete <111> set. 8 directions -> exactly 3 bits.
geometry_basis.WHY_NOT_OCTAHEDRAL_SITE: An octahedral site has 6 nearest neighbours along <100>. Si does not occupy one. Deriving 8 states from a 6-coordinate site is what forced v1 to pad its encoding map with two non-directional states.

constraints.geometry_validity: state must map to a canonical <111> direction

tensor_definition.NOTE: the state is an ORIENTATION, so it is carried by the eigenVECTORS. The eigenvalue spectrum is rotation-invariant and cannot distinguish these 8 states from one another — see silicon_error_correction.json, invariant_blindness.

encoding_map.GRAY_NOTE: codes are Gray-ordered within each sublattice so that adjacent bond directions differ in one bit, per CLAUDE.md development guideline 3.
encoding_map.REPLACES_v1: v1 named 6 octahedron directions (North/South apex, East/West ridge, Front/Back face) and padded to 8 with 'Axial symmetry' and 'Stable equilibrium node', which are not directions at all. The padding is the visible symptom of deriving 8 from a 6-fold site.
encoding_map.INVERSION_NOTE: inversion partners (000<->110, 001<->111, 011<->101, 010<->100) are uniformly Hamming-2 apart: physically antipodal directions are consistently 2 bits apart, while adjacent bonds within a sublattice are 1 bit apart.

read.method: polarization-resolved Raman, Si-Si optical phonon 520.7 cm^-1
read.reads: strain eigenvalues from peak splitting; eigenvector orientation from the polarization dependence via Oh Raman tensor selection rules

write.method: optomechanical — photoelastic coupling plus radiation pressure in a Si nanobeam photonic crystal
write.scope_limit: addresses MODE-scale strain over ~1e8 unit cells. Does NOT address individual lattice sites: the diffraction limit in Si is lambda/2n = 223 nm at 1.55 um against a 0.543 nm lattice constant.

REMOVED_v1.why_removed: Si is diamagnetic, chi ~ -3.4e-6, and Si-28 (92% abundant) has nuclear spin I=0. There is no magnetisation M for B_ext to couple to, so E_mag = -M : B_ext is identically zero. A 0.01 T stability field stabilises nothing. This is the same fault as Silicon_Error_Correction v1 and 3D_LIGHT_ENHANCED_OCTAHEDRAL_PROCESSING — three files, one wrong premise.

outputs.transition_energy_note: h x 1 THz = 4.14 meV. Retained from v1: the frequency_range was the authoritative source and remains plausible for a phonon-scale reorientation. It is NOT a Zeeman splitting, which is what v1 implied.
outputs.timescale_scope: elastic/phonon reorientation only. Thermal defect migration is Arrhenius and ~3.6 us at 300K — six orders slower. See silicon_error_correction.json, mechanisms.

falsifiers: OSE-1 a 9th distinguishable orientation state in unstrained diamond-cubic Si -> the <111> derivation is incomplete
OSE-2 state discrimination from the eigenvalue spectrum alone, with no eigenvector measurement -> the invariant-blindness claim is wrong (same as SIL-1)
OSE-3 measurable Zeeman splitting of these states at 0.01 T in undoped Si -> the magnetic deletion is wrong (same as LO-3)
OSE-4 reorientation between sublattice-A and sublattice-B states without breaking a bond -> the two sets are not inversion partners as claimed

FATAL: read_write_interface was 'magnetic field coupling (Zeeman basis)' with E_mag = -M : B_ext. Si is diamagnetic; M is zero; the equation evaluates to zero for any B_ext. The encoder had no working read or write channel.
HIGH: geometry_basis 'tetrahedral -> octahedral hybrid lattice' conflates the Td site with the Oh crystal. Si occupies a Td site; there is no octahedral site to hybridise with.

8 states were derived from octahedral coordination, which is 6-fold. The encoding_map shows the strain: 6 directional states plus 2 non-directional fillers ('Axial symmetry', 'Stable equilibrium node') to reach 8.
encoding_map state 101 was 'Back face - magnetic bias', a state defined by a mechanism that does not exist.
MED: codes were not Gray-ordered, so adjacent physical states could differ in up to 3 bits — contrary to the repository's own stability convention.
SURVIVED: 8 states / 3 bits is correct, for a different reason than stated.
109.47 deg is correct and is the intra-sublattice bond angle.
transition energy 0.0006626 aJ and the 0.2-3 ps timescale remain plausible for phonon-scale reorientation.

metadata.linked_NOTE: RESOLVED — Silicon_Error_Correction v2.0 flagged a possible Td/Oh mismatch here. It was real. This encoder was modelling neither site correctly; it is now indexed by <111> bond directions, which is Td-site symmetry plus the inversion that makes the crystal Oh.
